# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👎]

I see a blue light, display 0, and three wires ordered red, yellow, blue. Mute’s 👍👎 gesture has no established meaning yet, so I will provide the full observable state verbally to both monkeys; Blind can hear it and Mute can correlate it with the manual.

``` 
speak(text="Bomb view: display reads 0. Light is blue. Wires in order: 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]

The display and wires are unchanged, but the light is now orange. Mute sent the single gesture ✌, which Blind cannot see, so I should relay its named symbol aloud along with the updated visual state.

``` 
speak(text="Update: light is orange; display remains 0; wires remain 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Mute gestured: ✌.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]

The light has changed to yellow; display and wire order remain the same. Mute again signalled ✌. Since Blind cannot see that gesture, I will relay it and the current visual state aloud.

```
speak(text="Update: light is yellow; display 0; wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Mute again gestured: ✌.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]

The light is now red, with the display still at 0 and the wires still red, yellow, blue. Mute has repeated ✌ for three consecutive light changes; that likely carries a manual instruction, but its meaning has not been established for Blind. I will report the current state and repetition.

```
speak(text="Update: light is red; display 0; wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Mute has gestured ✌ on each of the last three turns.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌ 🤟]

The light is green, while the display and wire order remain unchanged. Blind has gestured ☝ ✌ 🤟, which only I and Mute can see, so I will forward those exact symbols to Mute. Mute’s repeated ✌ is invisible to Blind, so I will also report it aloud with the visual state.

``` 
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝", "✌", "🤟"])
speak(to="blind", text="Current view: green light, display 0, wires 1 red 2 yellow 3 blue. Mute again gestured ✌.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌ 🤟]

The light has cycled back to blue; display 0 and the wire order remain unchanged. Blind repeated ☝ ✌ 🤟, so I will relay that gesture to Mute again. I will tell Blind the current visual state and that Mute again made the same one-symbol gesture, without assuming its meaning.

```text
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝", "✌", "🤟"])
speak(to="blind", text="Current view: blue light, display 0, wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Mute again made the same single gesture as before.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍 👍]

The light is orange again; the display remains 0 and the wires remain red, yellow, blue. Blind’s new gesture sequence 👍 👍 👍 is visible to Mute through me, so I will pass it on. I will also give Blind the updated visual state.

``` 
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "👍", "👍"])
speak(to="blind", text="Current view: orange light, display 0, wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue.")
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍 👍]

The light is yellow; nothing else visible has changed. Blind has repeated the three-thumbs-up gesture, which Mute needs to receive directly through my relay. I will send it to Mute and update Blind on the visual state.

```text
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "👍", "👍"])
speak(to="blind", text="Current view: yellow light, display 0, wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue.")
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍 👍]

The light is red; display 0 and wire order red, yellow, blue are unchanged. Mute’s new two-thumbs-up gesture must be relayed to Blind, while Blind’s repeated three-thumbs-up gesture must be relayed to Mute. I will also provide Blind the current visual state.

```text
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "👍", "👍"])
speak(to="blind", text="Current view: red light, display 0, wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Mute gestured 👍 👍.")
```

TURN 10
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👍 ✌ 👍 👍 🤟 👍 👍 👍]

The light is green, with display 0 and wire order red, yellow, blue unchanged. Blind’s longer gesture sequence is likely important feedback for Mute to interpret against the manual, so I will relay it exactly. Blind also needs the current visible state.

```text
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝", "👍", "✌", "👍", "👍", "🤟", "👍", "👍", "👍"])
speak(to="blind", text="Current view: green light, display 0, wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue.")
```

TURN 11
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌ 🤟]

The visual state has returned to blue, still with display 0 and wires ordered red, yellow, blue. Mute again sent 👍 👍, which Blind cannot see, and Blind sent ☝ ✌ 🤟, which Mute needs relayed.

```text
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝", "✌", "🤟"])
speak(to="blind", text="Current view: blue light, display 0, wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Mute again gestured 👍 👍.")
```
